chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar and Bureyd ibn Muawiya, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no problem with standing upon the prayer mat made of hair and wool, when one prostrates on the ground. And if it is made from the growth of the earth, then there is no problem with standing upon it and prostrating upon it.

key_terms.الْمُصَلَّى: Prayer mat or place of prostration

ai.seo_question: What materials are permissible for a prayer mat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of various prayer mat materials by distinguishing between animal-based products, which require direct contact with the earth for the forehead, and plant-based products, which are fully permissible for both standing and prostration. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical connection to the earth (turabah) during sujood, ensuring the ritual purity and validity of the prostration gesture.
